Around national signing day and the spring game last year, when I was still on Reddit, I posted a prediction that Adam Griffith would make an amazing, pivotal kick in 2016, most likely a game winner. I was convinced that although he would struggle at times (he did), and he would piss a lot of fans off (like me), he would come through in a crucial moment.

When he kicked the [55 yarder vs LSU](http://www.al.com/sports/index.ssf/2015/11/watch_the_55-yard_field_goal_b.html), I figured that was it. It was a great kick in a close game right before halftime, but since I had already told Reddit to go fuck itself I didn't go back and call attention to it. I figured I'd wait and see if he hit a real game winner or something.

After the Iron Bowl (i.e. Six Kicks), I sort of felt like my specific prediction was turning into more of a blanket statement about the type of season this kid would have. He'd really improved since those awful games at the beginning of the year, when the only thing keeping us from stringing him up by his testicles and beating him with sticks was the tearjerking special by ESPN about him being an East Block orphan etc. You just can't do that to orphans.

Well, last night he made [the kick](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bY3c4P_MjsE) I predicted...sort of.

That onside kick was the ballsiest of ballsy play calls, not only because it could've given that freak Deshaun Watson a short field, but because Saban was resting the fate of that entire play on the shoulders of a guy who...and let's be fair here...is probably the least trustworthy kicker we've had since Saban arrived. Rather than collapse under pressure and squib it out of bounds, Griffith kicked as close to a perfect onside kick as I can imagine kicking, and it immediately hit me that this was the moment I'd felt was coming all along....sort of.

By "sort of," I mean that I had the feeling it would be a last minute field goal to go up by one point in a close game with a mediocre conference opponent, like Arkansas or Mississippi State. That's what it "felt" like when I posted it. Instead, Griffith exceeded my expectations. I got 7 points a few plays later instead of just 3, and we won a championship instead of just another game.

I was vindicated....sort of.

Unfortunately, I deleted my account last month, and also [overwrote all my comments with a greasemonkey script](https://voat.co/v/MeanwhileOnReddit/comments/743319), so my prediction won't even show up as "deleted" now. Oh the irony. Reddit is finally useful for something again, and I can't even utilize it.
